rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Every organic reaction starts with a bond breaking, and there are exactly two ways. **Homolytic fission** divides the shared pair **equally** — **A–B → A· + B·** — creating neutral **free radicals** with unpaired electrons; it favours non-polar bonds and needs **heat or light** (Cl₂ → 2Cl· in sunlight, starting the chain chlorination of methane).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Homolysis: A–B → A· + B· (e.g. Cl₂ → 2Cl·) - Heterolysis: A–B → A⁺ + :B⁻ (e.g. (CH₃)₃C–Cl → (CH₃)₃C⁺ + Cl⁻) - Carbocation: 6 valence electrons, positive; carbanion: 8, negative; radical: 7, neutral

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ All cells look the same under a microscope. ✅ Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have them.  ·  ❌ DNA and RNA are identical in structure. ✅ DNA is double-stranded with deoxyribose and thymine; RNA is single-stranded with ribose and uracil.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***One bond, two destinies*** — the C–Cl bond of tert-butyl chloride gives ions in water (heterolysis, substitution proceeds), while the Cl–Cl bond gives radicals in sunlight (homolysis, chlorination proceeds): the same chlorine, two different reaction worlds.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Homo = equal = radicals (light/heat, non-polar); hetero = unequal = ions (polar bond, polar solvent). Radical neutral 7e; carbocation 6e positive; carbanion negative. Arrows: full head pair, fishhook single electron.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): What is homolytic fission? Explain with an example.** — **Homolytic fission (homolysis)** is the breaking of a covalent bond in which the **shared electron pair is divided equally** between the two bonded atoms, each fragment receiving **one electron**.…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): What is heterolytic fission? Explain with an example.** — **Heterolytic fission (heterolysis)** is bond breaking in which the **entire bonding electron pair is transferred to the more electronegative atom**, producing **a cation and an anion**: **A–B → A⁺ + :B⁻**.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The mode of fission selects the chemistry: split evenly and you get radicals running chain reactions; split unevenly and you get ions that attract or donate pairs — every mechanism is built from these two moves.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Mechanism: step-by-step bond breaking/making path; curly arrows — full head = electron pair, half head = single electron. Homolytic fission: pair splits equally -> free radicals (neutral, unpaired electron, 7e, paramagnetic); A-B -> A. + B.; favoured by non-polar bonds + heat/light; Cl2 -> 2Cl.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Radical chain reactions (initiation, propagation, termination) explain everything from methane chlorination to polymer manufacture and atmospheric ozone chemistry.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Distinguish between a free radical, a carbocation and a carbanion.** — A **free radical** is a **neutral** species with an **unpaired electron** (seven electrons on carbon; paramagnetic), produced by **homolytic fission** — e.g. Cl· or CH₃·.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — How Bonds Break and Why It Matters Every organic reaction begins with a covalent bond breaking. **How** it breaks decides everything downstream: **homolytic fission** splits the pair equally, creating **free radicals**; **heterolytic fission** gives both electrons to one atom, creating **ions** (carbocation + anion).…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 What a reaction mechanism is - A **mechanism** is the **step-by-step description** of a reaction: which bonds break, which form, in what order, through which intermediates, catalysed how. - Electron movement is shown with **curly arrows**: full-head arrow = a **pair** of electrons moves; half-head (fishhook) = a **single electron** moves.…  ·  ## 3. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Mitosis produces genetically different cells. ✅ Mitosis produces genetically identical diploid daughter cells.  ·  ❌ Meiosis produces identical cells. ✅ Meiosis produces 4 genetically diverse haploid gametes.  ·  ❌ Crossing over occurs in mitosis. ✅ Crossing over occurs in Prophase I of meiosis only.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ All enzymes are proteins. ✅ Most enzymes are proteins; some RNA molecules (ribozymes) also have catalytic activity.  ·  ❌ ATP is the only energy currency. ✅ GTP, UTP, and CTP also serve as energy carriers in specific pathways.  ·  ❌ Photosynthesis occurs in all plant cells. ✅ Photosynthesis occurs only in cells containing chloroplasts (mainly mesophyll).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Respiration and photosynthesis are opposite processes with same equation. ✅ They are complementary but occur in different organelles and under different conditions.  ·  ❌ Oxygen is produced during respiration. ✅ Oxygen is consumed in aerobic respiration; produced during photosynthesis.  ·  ❌ Food chain shows all feeding relationships. ✅ Food chain is linear; food web shows interconnected feeding relationships.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ 90% of energy is transferred to next trophic level. ✅ Only ~10% energy transfers; ~90% lost as heat.  ·  ❌ Biomagnification decreases toxin concentration up the food chain. ✅ Biomagnification increases toxin concentration at higher trophic levels.  ·  ❌ Carbon cycle only involves plants and animals. ✅ Carbon cycle involves atmosphere, oceans, fossils, rocks, and decomposers.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Nitrogen fixation only occurs in bacteria. ✅ Some lightning and industrial processes (Haber) also fix nitrogen.  ·  ❌ All fungi are harmful. ✅ Many fungi are beneficial (decomposers, mycorrhizae, food, antibiotics like penicillin).  ·  ❌ Viruses are living organisms. ✅ Viruses are acellular — they cannot reproduce without a host and lack metabolism.
